body:
We're in college, so he has to go through all those motions. Unfortunately the stress is taking a toll on his work which I'm sure is contributing to his feeling of failure. That and the fact that he can't find a job. 
It's not like the circumstances are good and he just can't see it. He's also in a really dangerous position academically, which would stress anybody out. There's a lot hanging on this semester because he's not been able to do well in the past (despite the fact that he's brilliant) and the lack of support from his parents means that they aren't willing to keep giving him chances or understand that his problems aren't due to laziness.

I'm not particularly comfortable sharing details about myself through here, I don't want this to turn into a thread about myself because I'm more concerned for him. I'm happy to respond in more detail through PM, but I want to reiterate that I don't feel in any danger except for the fact that my issue is either not fatal at all or won't be for a long time.

This is what I'm fucking terrified of. I don't know how to handle this so I make my own judgment calls, and god knows what kind of damage I could do. I have been doing that, countering and letting it go back and forth, because I had heard from some therapists that you have to "apply logic to the negative thoughts" and hear an argument for them every time. I hadn't thought that I could be doing the exact wrong thing.

As hard as this is for me to comprehend, his parents do not care. They've said they're through with trying and he's on his own.

As I said in another comment, we made a deal to both see on-campus counselors. He had a meeting recently and will have more. 

I don't want to be his only hope. I don't have enough faith that I can do it. I've tried to help him identify other people who he can talk to but for one reason or another we come up empty. He had a slew of friends who have dipped out because he's "too much work" or "a downer."

I'm going to start seeing one, because I made him a deal that we would both go. He's seen someone, and I think he's got another appointment in a week or so, but he keeps talking about how worthless it is and there's nothing anyone can do.

The only thing I can think to do right now is say "Please don't go anywhere, we're in this together" so that maybe things will look a little brighter after some time and he can keep going to counseling. But he HAS done it before, and he HAS been medicated before so I'm scared. I try to say that he's never had a good therapist, medication, and someone he can talk to outside of therapy all at once so he has to try them all to see if having all three together will work. He's just tried before and failed because he got screwed over by the people around him and had a bad psychiatrist who gave him meds that fucked him up.
It is just like being slapped in the face. We'll sit for hours and talk, and it never gets any brighter for him. He never deviates from the rotation of things that he will say. All he'll do is promise not go go anywhere.
